newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - August 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - August 6.

-- HAMPEL WILL DRAFT 'SUPERCODE' OF GOVERNANCE RULES

The Hampel committee's interim report on corporate governance, lead by Sir Ronald Hampel, chairman of Imperial Chemical Industries, was published yesterday and outlines plans to merge recommendations for corporate governance in conjunction with the previous reports from the Cadbury committee on corporate governance and the Greenbury committee on executive pay. However Sir Ronald was not yet sure which parts of all the three reports to retain to form a single set of principles.
-- LI KA-SHING BUYS STAKES IN JARDINE GROUP

Hong Kong's most powerful businessman Li Ka-shing has bought stakes worth a combined HK$396m (31m stg) in two of the UK-controlled Jardine Matheson group companies, Jardine Matheson and Hongkong Land, giving him a 3 per cent stake in the group which he earlier attempted to takeover in 1987 and 1988. Share prices soared 20 per cent for Hongkong Land and 11 per cent for Jardine Matheson following the news.
-- HMV AND VIRGIN TO START SALE OF RECORDS ON INTERNET

Two of the UK's largest music retailers, HMV and WH Smith-owned Virgin, have announced plans to sell records, CD's, videos and other entertainment products directly over the internet in direct competition with US music retailers CDnow and Tower Records who already sell music products on the web. The move may spark record companies to bypass retailers and sell their records direct from their own web pages.
-- BRUSSELS FACES US TRADE ROW OVER 'MAD COW' RULES

European Union regulations to ban certain parts of meat products, namely cattle brain and spinal cord, has caused a huge trade uproar over the production of tallow, which includes these banned products, because the tallow is used in 80 per cent of pharmaceutical products and in the production of lubricants, tyres, packaging and printing ink. In addition to pressure from industry groups to alter the rules the US has threatened to complain to the World Trade Organisation over the impending ban on the US's $100m tallow exports to the EU.
-- STRONG POUND HITS SERVICE SECTOR GROWTH RATE

The Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply announced the results of its latest monthly survey revealing that the service industry is beginning to suffer under the strength of the pound, as much as the manufacturing industry, with a small decline in the growth of new business. The Office for Natioanl Statistics however have stated that the strength of sterling has not had any obvious effect upon levels of manufacturing production whilst the Royal Bank of Scotland said manufacturing 'was' suffering from the sterling effect.
-- MILD EUPHORIA AFTER BREWERS' LAGER OFFENSIVE

Traditional dark beer producers that make beers such as 'mild' and 'porter' have been optimistic about a resurgence in the wake of zealous promotion of 'disco' beers and lagers by large breweries, according to director of the Campaign for Real Ale Stephen Cox. The Great British Beer Festival at London's Olympia this week has been organised by Camra who claim that dark beer brewers are on the increase.
-- ICL WINS 160M STG BG CONTRACT

Information Technology systems and services company ICL has won a 160m stg, five year contract to manage the telecommunications business of Transco, the former British Gas GAS.L BG subsidiary pipeline business. The contract includes transferring Transco's microwave radio network of 300 radio masts and the network management system.
-- UBS DISPUTE ON INVESTMENT STANCE

Following the announcement of first-half results of a 67 per cent increase in net income to SFr186bn, the largest Swiss bank UBS has revealed that poor investment performance at its UK fund management subsidiary PDFM will change with a strategy rethink away from investment mainly in cash rather than equities. The announcement runs contrary to the beliefs of PDFM executives who maintain that there will only be a slight change in strategy but the firm will continue to invest heavily in cash.
-- LONDON CASINO BID RULED ANTI-COMPETITIVE

The Department of Trade and Industry has followed the advice of the Monopolies and Mergers Commission to stop the second hostile takeover bid of Capital Corporation by London Clubs International to form the largest up- market casino company because the initiative is not in the interests of competition. Share prices in both companies fell with London Clubs down 4 per cent and Capital down 10 per cent following the move.
-- GLAXO PAYMENT PUSHES CANTAB INTO THE BLACK

Biotechnology company Cantab Pharmaceuticals has announced pre-tax profit of 1.97m stg, compared to a loss of 3.7m stg for the first-half of last year, following a one-off payment from Glaxo Wellcome of 11m stg in licence fees and equity investment to support development of a new vaccine for genital herpes. Cantab chief executive Jurek Sikorski said that the company could run for three years on current investments without seeking further funds.
